In one second, every I.V. line on this patient tells me if it's safe for it.
Meet Maya. She's an I.C.U. nurse.
Her patient has four drugs, running through four tubes, into one tangle.
Before every push, she has to answer two questions.
And will my drug react with what's already in it?
Today, she traces tubes with gloved fingers, and checks a chart across the room. Many times a shift. Every shift.
So we built Lumen. A Lens for Snap Specs, running right here, in Lens Studio.
At the bedside, Lumen is quiet. Just faint dots on the ports.
She picks up furosemide, and every port answers.
Green: safe. Red: and it tells her why.
She pinches the red one. Lumen lights that exact tube, through the tangle, all the way to its pump.
Midazolam. Don't push here. And it points to the port that is safe.
Done. Logged. And the Lens goes quiet.
Behind her, out of view, a pump alarms. A chime and an arrow turn her head.
The line glows amber, right to the kink. She fixes it. Resolved.
And at shift change, one pinch on the I.V. pole walks every line. Bag, to pump, to port.
It sees what she sees. It draws on the real tube, not on a screen. And her hands never leave the syringe.
We designed Lumen to stay silent until it matters, and to put every answer on the thing it's about.
Our coding agent built it in Lens Studio, through the Lens Studio M.C.P. And Snap's LEAF tests pinch every control, for real.
Ten of ten pass in the preview.
Next: barcode scanning, real line tracking, live pump data.
Lumen. The right line. The safe port. Where you look.
